```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Shared data and helpers for every widget on this page ----
// The six counties come from R (see the hidden ojs_define() chunk in
// section 1), so widget values always match the real nc data.

// Colors used across widgets (same ink/red/blue/orange/green as Session 4)
col = ({
  ink: "#33414d", line: "#c9d1d8", head: "#eef1f4", fill: "#bcd3e6",
  muted: "#9aa5ad", red: "#d1495b", blue: "#1f5f8b", orange: "#e08a1e",
  green: "#5b8c5a", keyHead: "#fde9c8"
})

// ojs_define() may hand a single string over as a length-1 array
nc6 = {
  const raw = Array.isArray(nc6json) ? nc6json[0] : nc6json;
  return JSON.parse(raw).features.map(f => ({...f.properties, shape: f}));
}
county = Object.fromEntries(nc6.map(d => [d.NAME, d]))

// CSS transitions (not d3 transitions): they run without a JavaScript
// animation loop and show up in headless screenshots (Session 4 norm 3.6)
fade = "opacity 0.6s ease"
glide = "transform 0.9s ease, opacity 0.6s ease"

// Draw one county outline inside a cell. geoIdentity is planar, so the
// ring direction of the polygon doesn't matter (spherical d3 projections
// would fill the whole globe for a counter-clockwise ring).
drawShape = (g, feature, x, y, w, h) => {
  const proj = d3.geoIdentity().reflectY(true)
    .fitExtent([[x + 5, y + 3], [x + w - 5, y + h - 3]], feature);
  g.append("path").attr("d", d3.geoPath(proj)(feature))
    .attr("fill", col.fill).attr("stroke", col.blue).attr("stroke-width", 0.8);
}

// Draw a table into an SVG parent.
//   cols: [{key, label, w}]; rows: array of objects.
//   A "geometry" column draws the county shape (or EMPTY if none);
//   null/undefined values print as a red NA, like R does.
// Each cell group gets the class col-<key>, so a whole column can be faded.
// Rows are positioned with a CSS transform, so they can glide to new slots.
drawTable = (parent, {x, y, cols, rows, rowH = 26, title = null, keyCol = null}) => {
  const g = parent.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${x},${y})`);
  // Left edge of each column (plus the table's right edge at the end)
  const xs = Array.from(d3.cumsum([0, ...cols.map(c => c.w)]));
  if (title) {
    g.append("text").attr("x", 0).attr("y", -8).attr("font-size", 13)
      .attr("font-weight", 600).attr("fill", col.ink).text(title);
  }
  // Header row (the key column gets an orange header)
  const head = g.append("g").attr("class", "head");
  cols.forEach((c, j) => {
    const cell = head.append("g").attr("class", `col-${c.key}`).style("transition", fade);
    cell.append("rect").attr("x", xs[j]).attr("width", c.w).attr("height", rowH)
      .attr("fill", c.key === keyCol ? col.keyHead : col.head).attr("stroke", col.line);
    cell.append("text").attr("x", xs[j] + 6).attr("y", rowH / 2 + 4.5)
      .attr("font-size", 12.5).attr("font-family", "monospace").attr("font-weight", 600)
      .attr("fill", col.ink).text(c.label ?? c.key);
  });
  // Body rows
  const rowGs = rows.map((r, i) => {
    const rg = g.append("g").attr("class", "row")
      .style("transform", `translate(0px, ${(i + 1) * rowH}px)`).style("transition", glide);
    cols.forEach((c, j) => {
      const cell = rg.append("g").attr("class", `col-${c.key}`).style("transition", fade);
      cell.append("rect").attr("x", xs[j]).attr("width", c.w).attr("height", rowH)
        .attr("fill", "#fff").attr("stroke", col.line);
      const v = r[c.key];
      const txt = cell.append("text").attr("x", xs[j] + 6).attr("y", rowH / 2 + 4.5)
        .attr("font-size", 12.5).attr("font-family", "monospace");
      if (c.key === "geometry") {
        if (v) { txt.remove(); drawShape(cell, v, xs[j], 0, c.w, rowH); }
        else txt.attr("fill", col.muted).attr("font-style", "italic").text("EMPTY");
      } else if (v === null || v === undefined) {
        txt.attr("fill", col.red).attr("font-weight", 700).text("NA");
      } else {
        txt.attr("fill", col.ink).text(v);
      }
    });
    return rg;
  });
  return {g, rowGs, xs, rowH, width: xs[cols.length]};
}

// A curved connector between a left-table row and a right-table row
// ("tentacle"). It starts undrawn: pathLength = 1 makes one dash cover the
// whole curve, so moving stroke-dashoffset from 1 to 0 draws it on.
connector = (parent, x1, y1, x2, y2, color) => parent.append("path")
  .attr("class", "tentacle")
  .attr("d", `M${x1},${y1} C${(x1 + x2) / 2},${y1} ${(x1 + x2) / 2},${y2} ${x2},${y2}`)
  .attr("pathLength", 1)
  .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", color).attr("stroke-width", 2)
  .style("stroke-dasharray", "1").style("stroke-dashoffset", "1")
  .style("transition", "stroke-dashoffset 0.9s ease")
```

## Today

- Say how an **sf object** differs from a **data frame**, and why its
  geometry is **sticky**
- **Subset** rows and columns with base R and `dplyr`, and predict what
  comes out
- Define **joins**: **keys**, **inner** vs. **left**, and **cardinality**
- Choose a **linking field** that will actually match

## 1 Data frames and sf objects

- Data: **North Carolina counties** (`nc`), included with `sf`
- 100 counties, births (`BIR74`, `BIR79`) and sudden infant deaths (`SID74`,
  `SID79`)

```{r}
#| message: false
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

nc <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)

# The same data without the map, as a plain data frame
nc_df <- st_drop_geometry(nc)

class(nc)
class(nc_df)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
# Instructor-only: hand the first six counties (attributes + outlines) to
# the OJS widgets as GeoJSON text, so the widgets show real nc values.
nc6_js <- nc |>
  slice(1:6) |>
  select(NAME, FIPS, BIR74, SID74, BIR79, SID79)
gj_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
st_write(nc6_js, gj_file, quiet = TRUE)
ojs_define(nc6json = paste(readLines(gj_file), collapse = ""))
```

### An sf object is a data frame with a map attached

- **sf object** = a data frame + one **geometry column** (the shapes)
- Its class is **both**: `"sf"` and `"data.frame"`, so data frame tools
  still work
- **Sticky geometry**: the geometry column stays unless you **drop it on
  purpose** (`st_drop_geometry()`)

|  | Data frame | sf object |
|---|---|---|
| **Look** | Rows and columns | Same, plus a **header** (geometry type, bounding box, CRS) and a `geometry` column |
| **Feel** | Every column is independent | Geometry **sticks** to its row through subsets and joins |
| **Functionality** | `dplyr` verbs, `[ ]`, `$` | All of those, plus `st_*()` functions, maps with `plot()`, a CRS |
| **Use case** | Tables with no location: a CDC PLACES CSV, a census table | Features on a map: tracts, counties, facilities |

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Predict

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Data frame vs. sf: one table, built once; the cell below fades the
// sf header and the geometry column in and out ----
dfSvg = {
  const W = 470, H = 250;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, W, H]).style("width", "100%").style("max-width", "560px");
  const cols = [
    {key: "NAME", w: 110}, {key: "FIPS", w: 66}, {key: "BIR74", w: 66},
    {key: "SID74", w: 60}, {key: "geometry", w: 80}
  ];
  const rows = nc6.map(d => ({...d, geometry: d.shape}));
  // The sf header that print() shows above the table
  const hdr = svg.append("g").attr("class", "sfhdr").style("transition", fade).attr("font-family", "monospace")
    .attr("font-size", 12).attr("fill", col.blue);
  hdr.append("text").attr("x", 10).attr("y", 16).text("Simple feature collection with 6 features and 4 fields");
  hdr.append("text").attr("x", 10).attr("y", 32).text("Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON");
  hdr.append("text").attr("x", 10).attr("y", 48).text("Geodetic CRS:  NAD27");
  drawTable(svg, {x: 10, y: 62, cols, rows});
  return html`<div class="widget">${svg.node()}
    <div class="op-box"><code class="df-code"></code><div class="op-out df-out"></div></div></div>`;
}
```

## 2 Subsetting: base R and `dplyr`

- **Rows** by condition: `filter()` or `x[condition, ]`
- **Rows** by position: `slice()` or `x[1:3, ]`
  - **Position is fragile**: row order can change; a condition says what you
    mean
- **Columns** by name: `select()` or `x[ , c("a", "b")]`
- **One column out** as a plain vector: `x$a` or `pull(x, a)`
  - **No geometry**: a vector isn't a table
- On an sf object, base R and `dplyr` give the **same result**

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Predict
- `nc6` has 6 counties and 4 attribute columns. Which column survives every
  operation that returns a table?
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// The operations shown in the widget.
//   crit:  the criterion in words, shown BEFORE the result
//   hlCols / hlRows: what the criterion refers to (highlighted in orange)
//   rows/cols: what the operation keeps; hdr: is the result still sf?
subsetOps = {
  const all = ["NAME", "FIPS", "BIR74", "SID74", "geometry"];
  const allRows = () => true;
  return [
    {name: "Start: the whole table", base: "nc6", tidy: "nc6",
     crit: "No criteria: the whole table", hlCols: [], hlRows: [],
     rows: allRows, cols: all, hdr: true,
     out: "sf · 6 rows × 5 columns (4 fields + geometry)"},
    {name: "Rows by condition", base: "nc6[nc6$BIR74 > 1400, ]", tidy: "filter(nc6, BIR74 > 1400)",
     crit: "Keep rows where BIR74 > 1400 · keep every column", hlCols: ["BIR74"], hlRows: [],
     rows: d => d.BIR74 > 1400, cols: all, hdr: true,
     out: "sf · 3 rows × 5 columns"},
    {name: "Rows by position", base: "nc6[1:3, ]", tidy: "slice(nc6, 1:3)",
     crit: "Keep rows 1 to 3 · keep every column", hlCols: [], hlRows: [0, 1, 2],
     rows: (d, i) => i < 3, cols: all, hdr: true,
     out: "sf · 3 rows × 5 columns"},
    {name: "Columns by name", base: 'nc6[ , c("NAME", "BIR74")]', tidy: "select(nc6, NAME, BIR74)",
     crit: "Keep every row · keep columns NAME and BIR74", hlCols: ["NAME", "BIR74"], hlRows: [],
     rows: allRows, cols: ["NAME", "BIR74", "geometry"], hdr: true,
     out: "sf · 6 rows × 3 columns: geometry came along without being asked"},
    {name: "Rows and columns", base: 'nc6[nc6$SID74 == 0, "NAME"]', tidy: "nc6 |> filter(SID74 == 0) |> select(NAME)",
     crit: "Keep rows where SID74 == 0 · keep column NAME", hlCols: ["SID74", "NAME"], hlRows: [],
     rows: d => d.SID74 === 0, cols: ["NAME", "geometry"], hdr: true,
     out: "sf · 1 row × 2 columns"},
    {name: "One column as a vector", base: "nc6$NAME", tidy: "pull(nc6, NAME)",
     crit: "Take column NAME out of the table", hlCols: ["NAME"], hlRows: [],
     rows: allRows, cols: ["NAME"], hdr: false,
     out: 'character vector, length 6: "Ashe" "Alleghany" "Surry" … (no table, no geometry)'},
    {name: "Drop the geometry", base: "st_drop_geometry(nc6)", tidy: "st_drop_geometry(nc6)",
     crit: "Remove the geometry column", hlCols: ["geometry"], hlRows: [],
     rows: allRows, cols: ["NAME", "FIPS", "BIR74", "SID74"], hdr: false,
     out: "data.frame · 6 rows × 4 columns: a plain table"}
  ];
}
viewof subsetOp = Inputs.radio(subsetOps.map(d => d.name), {value: subsetOps[0].name, label: "Operation"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// "Show result" button. Referencing subsetOp makes this cell re-run when
// the operation changes, which creates a fresh button (count back to 0),
// so every new operation starts at its criterion, not its result.
// Built by hand rather than with Inputs.button(), which rendered as a blank
// dark block under the site theme. The wrapper's value counts clicks.
viewof subsetReveal = {
  subsetOp;
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  const b = document.createElement("button");
  b.className = "btn btn-outline-primary btn-sm";
  b.textContent = "Show result →";
  wrap.appendChild(b);
  wrap.value = 0;
  b.addEventListener("click", () => {
    wrap.value += 1;
    wrap.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
  });
  return wrap;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Subsetting figure, built once ----
subsetSvg = {
  const W = 470, H = 250, T = {x: 34, y: 62}, rowH = 26;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, W, H]).style("width", "100%").style("max-width", "560px");
  const cols = [
    {key: "NAME", w: 110}, {key: "FIPS", w: 66}, {key: "BIR74", w: 66},
    {key: "SID74", w: 60}, {key: "geometry", w: 80}
  ];
  const rows = nc6.map(d => ({...d, geometry: d.shape}));
  const hdr = svg.append("g").attr("class", "sfhdr").style("transition", fade).attr("font-family", "monospace")
    .attr("font-size", 12).attr("fill", col.blue);
  hdr.append("text").attr("class", "hdr1").attr("x", 10).attr("y", 16);
  hdr.append("text").attr("x", 10).attr("y", 32).text("Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON");
  hdr.append("text").attr("x", 10).attr("y", 48).text("Geodetic CRS:  NAD27");
  // Row numbers, as R prints them (used by "Rows by position")
  rows.forEach((_, i) => svg.append("text").attr("class", "rownum")
    .attr("x", T.x - 8).attr("y", T.y + (i + 1.5) * rowH + 4.5).attr("text-anchor", "end")
    .attr("font-size", 12).attr("font-family", "monospace").attr("fill", col.muted)
    .style("transition", "opacity 0.6s ease, fill 0.4s ease").text(i + 1));
  drawTable(svg, {x: T.x, y: T.y, cols, rows});
  // Header cells change color when the criterion refers to them
  svg.selectAll(".head rect").style("transition", "fill 0.4s ease");
  // "sticky" tag that appears above the geometry column when it survives a
  // column subset nobody asked it to survive
  svg.append("text").attr("class", "sticky").attr("x", T.x + 302 + 40).attr("y", 58)
    .attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 12).attr("font-weight", 700)
    .attr("fill", col.orange).style("transition", fade).style("opacity", 0).text("sticky ↓");
  // Code, criteria and result go ABOVE the table, so the eye reads the
  // operation first and then looks down at what it does
  return html`<div class="widget">
    <div class="op-box op-box-top">
      <div><span class="op-tag">base R</span><code class="op-base"></code></div>
      <div><span class="op-tag">dplyr</span><code class="op-tidy"></code></div>
      <div><span class="op-tag">criteria</span><span class="op-crit"></span></div>
      <div class="op-out"></div>
    </div>${svg.node()}</div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- React to the operation and the button ----
// Before the click: show the criterion (code, words, orange highlights) on
// the full table. After the click: fade what's dropped and give the result.
{
  const op = subsetOps.find(d => d.name === subsetOp);
  const shown = subsetReveal > 0;
  const svg = d3.select(subsetSvg);
  const keepRow = nc6.map((d, i) => op.rows(d, i));
  const nKeep = shown ? keepRow.filter(Boolean).length : 6;
  const allCols = ["NAME", "FIPS", "BIR74", "SID74", "geometry"];
  const keptCols = shown ? op.cols : allCols;

  // Criterion highlights: column headers and row numbers it refers to
  allCols.forEach(k => svg.selectAll(`.head .col-${k} rect`)
    .style("fill", op.hlCols.includes(k) ? col.keyHead : col.head));
  svg.selectAll(".rownum").each(function(_, i) {
    d3.select(this).style("fill", op.hlRows.includes(i) ? col.orange : col.muted)
      .style("font-weight", op.hlRows.includes(i) ? 700 : 400)
      .style("opacity", !shown || keepRow[i] ? 1 : 0.12);
  });

  // Rows: dim the dropped ones (kept in place, so you can see what went)
  svg.selectAll(".row").each(function(_, i) {
    d3.select(this).style("opacity", !shown || keepRow[i] ? 1 : 0.12);
  });
  // Columns: dim the dropped ones, in the header and every row
  allCols.forEach(k => svg.selectAll(`.col-${k}`).style("opacity", keptCols.includes(k) ? 1 : 0.12));

  // The sf header only exists while the result is still an sf object
  const nFields = keptCols.filter(k => k !== "geometry").length;
  svg.select(".hdr1").text(`Simple feature collection with ${nKeep} feature${nKeep === 1 ? "" : "s"} and ${nFields} field${nFields === 1 ? "" : "s"}`);
  svg.select(".sfhdr").style("opacity", !shown || op.hdr ? 1 : 0.12);
  // Flag sticky geometry when columns were chosen and geometry wasn't one of them
  svg.select(".sticky").style("opacity", shown && op.hdr && op.cols.length < 5 ? 1 : 0);

  svg.select(".op-base").text(op.base);
  svg.select(".op-tidy").text(op.tidy);
  svg.select(".op-crit").text(op.crit);
  svg.select(".op-out").text(shown ? "→ " + op.out : "What comes out? Predict, then click Show result");
  return html`<span></span>`;
}
```

## 3 Joins: combining tables by a key

### Keys

- **Join**: add the columns of one table to another by **matching rows**
- **Key** (linking field): the column whose values must match in both
  tables, e.g. `FIPS`
- Rows match by **value**, not by **position**: the two tables can be in
  any order
- **Left** table = the first argument; **right** table = the second

### Inner vs. left

- **`inner_join()`**: keep only rows whose key is in **both** tables
- **`left_join()`**: keep **every row of the left** table; **NA** where
  the right table had no match
- `right_join()` and `full_join()` also keep unmatched rows **from the
  right** table, which have **no polygon** (**EMPTY** geometry)
- So with sf: **sf object on the left**, then **left** (keep every
  feature) or **inner** (keep only matched features)

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Predict
- Alleghany has no row in `births79`; Northampton has no polygon in
  `counties`. Which join keeps each one?
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
joinTypes = ["not joined", "inner_join", "left_join", "right_join", "full_join"]
viewof joinType = Inputs.radio(joinTypes, {value: "not joined", label: "Join"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Join types figure, built once. Left: 4 counties (sf). Right: births
// for 4 counties, in a different order, one of them not in the left table.
// Result: every row any join could produce; the cell below picks which
// ones show and slides them into place. Starts "not joined": no lines,
// no result. ----
joinGeom = {
  const leftNames = ["Ashe", "Alleghany", "Surry", "Currituck"];
  const rightNames = ["Surry", "Northampton", "Ashe", "Currituck"];
  // Result rows, in the order dplyr returns them: left rows first, then
  // right-only rows at the end
  const resultRows = [
    ...leftNames.map(n => ({NAME: n, FIPS: county[n].FIPS,
      BIR79: rightNames.includes(n) ? county[n].BIR79 : null, geometry: county[n].shape,
      inLeft: true, inRight: rightNames.includes(n)})),
    {NAME: null, FIPS: county.Northampton.FIPS, BIR79: county.Northampton.BIR79, geometry: null,
     inLeft: false, inRight: true}
  ];
  return {leftNames, rightNames, resultRows};
}

joinSvg = {
  const {leftNames, rightNames, resultRows} = joinGeom;
  const W = 600, H = 410, rowH = 26;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, W, H]).style("width", "100%").style("max-width", "700px");
  const L = {x: 10, y: 34}, R = {x: 440, y: 34};
  const left = drawTable(svg, {x: L.x, y: L.y, keyCol: "FIPS", title: "counties (sf)",
    cols: [{key: "NAME", w: 100}, {key: "FIPS", w: 66}, {key: "geometry", w: 70}],
    rows: leftNames.map(n => ({NAME: n, FIPS: county[n].FIPS, geometry: county[n].shape}))});
  const right = drawTable(svg, {x: R.x, y: R.y, keyCol: "FIPS", title: "births79 (data frame)",
    cols: [{key: "FIPS", w: 66}, {key: "BIR79", w: 66}],
    rows: rightNames.map(n => ({FIPS: county[n].FIPS, BIR79: county[n].BIR79}))});
  left.rowGs.forEach((g, i) => g.attr("data-name", leftNames[i]).attr("class", "row lrow"));
  right.rowGs.forEach((g, i) => g.attr("data-name", rightNames[i]).attr("class", "row rrow"));
  // Tentacles between matching keys (drawn on when a join is chosen), and
  // "no match" labels for the rows with nothing to reach
  const lx = L.x + left.width, rx = R.x;
  leftNames.forEach((n, i) => {
    const j = rightNames.indexOf(n);
    const y1 = L.y + (i + 1.5) * rowH;
    if (j >= 0) connector(svg, lx, y1, rx, R.y + (j + 1.5) * rowH, col.green);
    else svg.append("text").attr("class", "nomatch").attr("x", lx + 8).attr("y", y1 + 4).attr("font-size", 12)
      .attr("fill", col.orange).attr("font-weight", 600).style("opacity", 0).style("transition", fade).text("no match");
  });
  rightNames.forEach((n, j) => {
    if (!leftNames.includes(n)) svg.append("text").attr("class", "nomatch").attr("x", rx - 8).attr("y", R.y + (j + 1.5) * rowH + 4)
      .attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("font-size", 12).attr("fill", col.orange).attr("font-weight", 600)
      .style("opacity", 0).style("transition", fade).text("no match");
  });
  // Result table: all five candidate rows; the update cell positions them.
  // The whole result (title, header, rows) is hidden until a join is chosen.
  const res = drawTable(svg, {x: L.x, y: 220, keyCol: "FIPS", title: "result",
    cols: [{key: "NAME", w: 100}, {key: "FIPS", w: 66}, {key: "BIR79", w: 66}, {key: "geometry", w: 70}],
    rows: resultRows});
  res.g.attr("class", "result").style("opacity", 0).style("transition", fade);
  res.rowGs.forEach(g => g.attr("class", "row resrow"));
  return html`<div class="widget">${svg.node()}
    <div class="op-box"><code class="join-code"></code><div class="op-out join-out"></div></div></div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- React to the join type: draw the tentacles, then show which rows
// survive and slide them into place ----
{
  const {resultRows} = joinGeom;
  const rowH = 26;
  const joined = joinType !== "not joined";
  const svg = d3.select(joinSvg);
  // When coming from "not joined", wait for the tentacles before showing
  // the result; when switching between join types, update at once
  const wasJoined = joinSvg.__joined ?? false;
  joinSvg.__joined = joined;
  const delay = joined && !wasJoined ? "0.9s" : "0s";

  svg.selectAll(".tentacle").style("stroke-dashoffset", joined ? "0" : "1");
  svg.selectAll(".nomatch").style("transition-delay", delay).style("opacity", joined ? 1 : 0);
  svg.select(".result").style("transition-delay", delay).style("opacity", joined ? 1 : 0);

  // Which result rows each join keeps
  const keep = r => joinType === "inner_join" ? r.inLeft && r.inRight
    : joinType === "left_join" ? r.inLeft
    : joinType === "right_join" ? r.inRight
    : joinType === "full_join";
  // Slide kept rows into consecutive slots; hide the rest where they are
  let slot = 0;
  svg.selectAll(".resrow").each(function(_, i) {
    const k = keep(resultRows[i]);
    const g = d3.select(this).style("opacity", k ? 1 : 0);
    if (k) g.style("transform", `translate(0px, ${++slot * rowH}px)`);
  });
  // Dim source rows that don't make it into the result
  const leftKept = joinType === "inner_join" || joinType === "right_join" ? n => n !== "Alleghany" : () => true;
  const rightKept = joinType === "inner_join" || joinType === "left_join" ? n => n !== "Northampton" : () => true;
  svg.selectAll(".lrow").each(function() { d3.select(this).style("opacity", leftKept(this.dataset.name) ? 1 : 0.25); });
  svg.selectAll(".rrow").each(function() { d3.select(this).style("opacity", rightKept(this.dataset.name) ? 1 : 0.25); });

  const notes = {
    "not joined": "Two separate tables. Pick a join",
    inner_join: "only keys found in both tables · 3 rows",
    left_join: "every row of counties; NA where births79 had no match · 4 rows",
    right_join: "every row of births79; Northampton has no polygon (EMPTY) · 4 rows",
    full_join: "every row of both tables; one EMPTY polygon · 5 rows"
  };
  svg.select(".join-code").text(joined ? `${joinType}(counties, births79, by = "FIPS")` : "counties   births79");
  svg.select(".join-out").text("→ " + notes[joinType]);
  return html`<span></span>`;
}
```

- The **left** table decides what you start from; put the **sf object
  first**
- Table first, sf second: the result is a **plain data frame**, and the
  geometry is just a column

```{r}
# 25 counties with more than 5,000 births in 1979; one row per county
births79 <- nc_df |>
  filter(BIR79 > 5000) |>
  select(FIPS, BIR79)

counties <- select(nc, NAME, FIPS)

# sf first: still an sf object
sf_first <- left_join(counties, births79, by = "FIPS")
class(sf_first)

# Table first: the geometry comes along, but the result isn't sf anymore
table_first <- left_join(births79, counties, by = "FIPS")
class(table_first)
```

### Cardinality: how many matches per key?

- **Cardinality**: how many rows on each side share a key value
- **One-to-one**: each key once on each side → rows out = rows in
- **One-to-many**: a key repeats in the right table → **rows multiply**,
  and each polygon **repeats**
- `dplyr` **warns only for many-to-many**; one-to-many is **silent**

<!-- separate list -->

- Two right-hand tables for the same three counties:
  - **`births`**: births in 1979, **one row per county**
  - **`sids_long`**: SIDS deaths (sudden infant death syndrome) **per county
    per year**: one row for 1974 and one for 1979, so **two rows per county**
- "Long" format: one row per county **and year**, instead of one column per
  year (`SID74`, `SID79` in `nc`)

```{r}
# Build sids_long: one block of rows per year, stacked
sids74 <- nc_df |>
  select(FIPS, SIDS = SID74) |>
  mutate(year = 1974)
sids79 <- nc_df |>
  select(FIPS, SIDS = SID79) |>
  mutate(year = 1979)
sids_long <- bind_rows(sids74, sids79)

# Two rows per county: Ashe (37009) appears once per year
sids_long |>
  filter(FIPS == "37009")
nrow(sids_long)
```

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Predict
- Three counties; `sids_long` has **two rows per county**. How many rows
  come out of `left_join()`?
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
cardModes = ["not joined", "One-to-one: births", "One-to-many: sids_long"]
viewof cardMode = Inputs.radio(cardModes, {value: cardModes[0], label: "Join to"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Cardinality figure, built once. Both right tables are always shown;
// a join sends tentacles to one of them, then shows its result. In
// one-to-many mode the six result rows spread out from three slots, so each
// county visibly doubles. ----
cardSvg = {
  const names = ["Ashe", "Alleghany", "Surry"];
  // Layout: counties top left, births and sids_long stacked on the right,
  // and the result under counties, level with sids_long. The right tables
  // sit far enough right that the tentacles curve down past the result.
  const W = 720, H = 390, rowH = 26;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, W, H]).style("width", "100%").style("max-width", "780px");
  const L = {x: 10, y: 34}, B = {x: 540, y: 34}, S = {x: 540, y: 190}, Ry = 190;
  const left = drawTable(svg, {x: L.x, y: L.y, keyCol: "FIPS", title: "counties (sf)",
    cols: [{key: "NAME", w: 100}, {key: "FIPS", w: 66}, {key: "geometry", w: 70}],
    rows: names.map(n => ({NAME: n, FIPS: county[n].FIPS, geometry: county[n].shape}))});
  const lx = L.x + left.width;

  // births: one row per county
  const births = drawTable(svg, {x: B.x, y: B.y, keyCol: "FIPS", title: "births",
    cols: [{key: "FIPS", w: 66}, {key: "BIR79", w: 66}],
    rows: names.map(n => ({FIPS: county[n].FIPS, BIR79: county[n].BIR79}))});
  births.g.attr("class", "tbl-one").style("transition", fade);

  // sids_long: two rows per county (1974, 1979)
  const longRows = names.flatMap(n => [
    {NAME: n, FIPS: county[n].FIPS, year: 1974, SIDS: county[n].SID74, geometry: county[n].shape},
    {NAME: n, FIPS: county[n].FIPS, year: 1979, SIDS: county[n].SID79, geometry: county[n].shape}
  ]);
  const sids = drawTable(svg, {x: S.x, y: S.y, keyCol: "FIPS", title: "sids_long",
    cols: [{key: "FIPS", w: 66}, {key: "year", w: 50}, {key: "SIDS", w: 50}], rows: longRows});
  sids.g.attr("class", "tbl-many").style("transition", fade);

  // Tentacles: one per match, drawn on by the update cell
  const tOne = svg.append("g").attr("class", "t-one");
  names.forEach((n, i) => connector(tOne, lx, L.y + (i + 1.5) * rowH, B.x, B.y + (i + 1.5) * rowH, col.green));
  const tMany = svg.append("g").attr("class", "t-many");
  longRows.forEach((r, j) => connector(tMany, lx, L.y + (Math.floor(j / 2) + 1.5) * rowH,
    S.x, S.y + (j + 1.5) * rowH, col.orange));

  // Results, hidden until a join is chosen. One-to-one: 3 rows.
  // One-to-many: 6 rows; rows 2k and 2k+1 collapse onto slot k when hidden,
  // then spread apart when shown.
  const resOne = drawTable(svg, {x: L.x, y: Ry, keyCol: "FIPS", title: "left_join(counties, births, by = \"FIPS\")",
    cols: [{key: "NAME", w: 90}, {key: "FIPS", w: 60}, {key: "BIR79", w: 60}, {key: "geometry", w: 64}],
    rows: names.map(n => ({NAME: n, FIPS: county[n].FIPS, BIR79: county[n].BIR79, geometry: county[n].shape}))});
  resOne.g.attr("class", "res-one").style("opacity", 0).style("transition", fade);
  const resMany = drawTable(svg, {x: L.x, y: Ry, keyCol: "FIPS", title: "left_join(counties, sids_long, by = \"FIPS\")",
    cols: [{key: "NAME", w: 90}, {key: "FIPS", w: 60}, {key: "year", w: 46}, {key: "SIDS", w: 46}, {key: "geometry", w: 64}],
    rows: longRows});
  resMany.g.attr("class", "res-many").style("opacity", 0).style("transition", fade);
  resMany.rowGs.forEach(g => g.attr("class", "row manyrow"));
  return html`<div class="widget">${svg.node()}<div class="op-box"><div class="op-out card-out"></div></div></div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- React to the join choice: tentacles out, then the result ----
{
  const one = cardMode === cardModes[1], many = cardMode === cardModes[2];
  const rowH = 26;
  const svg = d3.select(cardSvg);
  // The result waits for the tentacles to finish drawing
  const delay = "0.9s";

  // Tentacles: draw the chosen set, retract the other
  svg.selectAll(".t-one .tentacle").style("stroke-dashoffset", one ? "0" : "1");
  svg.selectAll(".t-many .tentacle").style("stroke-dashoffset", many ? "0" : "1");
  // Both tables stay visible; the one not being joined dims
  svg.select(".tbl-one").style("opacity", many ? 0.3 : 1);
  svg.select(".tbl-many").style("opacity", one ? 0.3 : 1);
  // Results: hide at once, show after the tentacles
  svg.select(".res-one").style("transition-delay", one ? delay : "0s").style("opacity", one ? 1 : 0);
  svg.select(".res-many").style("transition-delay", many ? delay : "0s").style("opacity", many ? 1 : 0);
  svg.selectAll(".manyrow").each(function(_, i) {
    const slot = many ? i + 1 : Math.floor(i / 2) + 1;
    d3.select(this).style("transition-delay", many ? delay : "0s")
      .style("transform", `translate(0px, ${slot * rowH}px)`);
  });
  svg.select(".card-out").text(
    many ? "→ one-to-many: 3 counties in, 6 rows out. Each polygon now appears twice, and dplyr gives no warning"
    : one ? "→ one-to-one: 3 rows in, 3 rows out"
    : "→ Three counties, two possible tables. Pick one to join");
  return html`<span></span>`;
}
```

| Relationship | Example | Rows out | `dplyr` says |
|---|---|---|---|
| One-to-one | Counties + births, one row per county | Same as the left table | Nothing |
| One-to-many | Counties + SIDS by county **and year** | More; polygons repeat | **Nothing** |
| Many-to-one | Tracts + a county table, by county code | Same as the left table | Nothing (this one is normal) |
| Many-to-many | Repeated keys on **both** sides | Multiplies | A **warning** |

### Choosing your linking fields

- **Unique** on the side that should have one row per key:
  `anyDuplicated(births79$FIPS)` returns `0`
- **Same meaning**: county code ↔ county code, not county code ↔ some other
  ID
- **Same type**: character vs. numeric is a **loud error** (below)
- **Same format**: `"37009"` vs. `"1400000US37009"` is **no error**, just
  **no matches**
- **Codes over names**: names vary in spelling and punctuation ("St. Mary's"
  vs. "Saint Marys"); codes are built to match
- **Name the key**: always write `by = "FIPS"`; if the names differ,
  `by = c("FIPS" = "fips")`

```{r}
#| error: true
# FIPS is text ("37009"); FIPSNO is a number (37009)
births_num <- nc_df |>
  select(FIPSNO, BIR79)

left_join(counties, births_num, by = c("FIPS" = "FIPSNO"))
```

### Think-pair-share: how many rows?

- **Input** for all three:
  - `counties`: **sf**, **100 rows**, one per county; columns `NAME`, `FIPS`
  - `births79`: **data frame**, **25 rows**, one per county with more than
    5,000 births; columns `FIPS`, `BIR79`
  - `sids_long`: **data frame**, **200 rows**, **two per county** (1974,
    1979); columns `FIPS`, `SIDS`, `year`

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## 1. Left vs. inner.
```r
left_join(counties, births79, by = "FIPS")
inner_join(counties, births79, by = "FIPS")
```
- Rows from each? How many `NA`s in `BIR79` after the left join?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer 1
- **left: 100 rows**, with **75 `NA`s**: every county stays
- **inner: 25 rows**: only counties with a match

```{r}
with_left <- left_join(counties, births79, by = "FIPS")
nrow(with_left)
sum(is.na(with_left$BIR79))

with_inner <- inner_join(counties, births79, by = "FIPS")
nrow(with_inner)
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## 2. Two rows per county.
```r
left_join(counties, sids_long, by = "FIPS")
```
- How many rows? Any warning?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer 2
- **200 rows**, **no warning**: one-to-many, so every county polygon appears
  **twice**
- A map draws each county twice; a sum over counties counts each one twice

```{r}
# sids_long was built in the cardinality section above
with_years <- left_join(counties, sids_long, by = "FIPS")
nrow(with_years)
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## 3. Table first.
```r
left_join(births79, counties, by = "FIPS")
```
- How many rows? What class?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer 3
- **25 rows**, and a **plain data frame**: the left table was a data frame
- The geometry is still there as a column, but it's **not an sf object**:
  no header, no CRS, and `st_*()` functions won't treat it as a map

```{r}
flipped <- left_join(births79, counties, by = "FIPS")
nrow(flipped)
class(flipped)
```
:::

---

## 4 In your code

| Question | Code | What to look for |
|---|---|---|
| Is this a map or a table? | `class(x)` | `"sf"` first means map |
| How big is it? | `dim(x)`, `nrow(x)` | Compare **before and after** every subset and join |
| Is the key unique? | `anyDuplicated(tbl$key)` | `0` |
| Do the key types match? | `class(a$key)`, `class(b$key)` | The same class |
| Did rows match? | `sum(is.na(x$new_column))` | How many rows got `NA` |
| Did rows multiply? | `nrow()` before and after `left_join()` | Equal, unless you meant one-to-many |

- A join that runs is **not** a join that worked
- Most join problems **don't error**: they show up as **NAs** or **extra
  rows**
